title: Regulators are trying to protect you from being fired by AI – here’s how
key_facts: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 947, the "No Robo Bosses Act".
It bars employers from leaving disciplinary and termination decisions entirely to AI (automated decision systems).
Employers must check AI output and give the employee the reasons and data behind the decision.
The law takes effect on 1 July 2027; workers can complain to the California Labor Commissioner.
Employers must say whether a mass layoff, relocation or termination was caused by an AI system.
A lawyer, Lily Li, expects companies to find loopholes such as check-the-box reviews.
quote_evidence: SB 947, somewhat cheekily called the “No Robo Bosses Act,” prohibits employers from outsourcing disciplinary and termination decisions entirely to AI, referred to in the bill as automated decision systems (ADS).

The law, which goes into effect on July 1, 2027, lets affected employees file complaints with the California Labor Commissioner if they believe this process was not followed correctly in a firing decision.
why_it_matters_hint: First-in-the-US style human-review rule for AI firings; may set a template for other states.
event_date: signed about 29-30 Sep 2026 (CNBC coverage dated 30 Sep 2026, Fisher Phillips 1 Oct)
notes: ZDNET text gives no signing date ("recently signed"); search headlines (CNBC 30 Sep, KQED and Ogletree 1 Oct 2026) show it was signed in late September. This is an explainer of older news; score lowered two.
